features.source_location: Effective EC3 primary PDF physical 117 / printed 102: §7.7.3.1 says the page tree defines page order and processors shall be prepared for any tree form built from the specified node types. Physical 118 / printed 103 begins Table 30 required node entries, including indirect Kids and writer-consistent Count. No relevant EC3 amendment to the any-form sentence found in doc/errata-read.md.
features.ledger: Rows 7.7.3, 7.7.3.1, 7.7.3.2 marked implemented; prior page_resources_current audit does not certify every tree form and explicitly leaves graph/bounds unaudited.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-model/src/page.rs: MAX_TREE_DEPTH=64; `find_leaf`, `reaches_a_page`, `count_leaves`, and `every_leaf` stop after the bound. When the probe fails, `Pages::new` performs additive object scan recovery; `found_by_scanning` exposes it. `crates/viewer-core/src/notes.rs::about` reports that the tree leads to no page and gives the count found by scan; for a valid over-depth tree the “leads to no page” clause is inaccurate, though the scan/order is disclosed.
features.existing_assertions: page_geometry::a_page_tree_of_any_shape_yields_its_pages_in_the_order_its_kids_arrays_give and page_tree_nodes.rs cover common branching/unbalanced shapes, exact order, and damaged cycles. I found no valid unary tree over the depth boundary. Existing cycle test is malformed input and cannot stand in for this case.
features.assessment: Confirmed B48: depth64 keeps Kids order; depth65 returns both pages in object-number order. Recovery is disclosed, so this is not silent truncation. A truthful explicit resource-limit refusal may be an acceptable future response; changed successful page order does not follow the source-defined ordering.
